sources.cite: Microsoft Learn, Overview of Log Replay Service with Azure SQL Managed Instance
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: LRS 'scans all files placed in the Azure Blob Storage account and constructs the backup chain from reading the file headers'; each database's backups go in its own folder, 'Don't use nested folders inside database folders, because nested-folder structure isn't supported'; in continuous mode the cutover is: stop the workload, take the log-tail backup, upload it, 'Confirm the log-tail backup is shown as restored', then run the complete operation (az sql midb log-replay complete); 'Stopping the operation deletes the database that you're restoring'; after completion, more backups cannot be restored without starting over. The az sql midb log-replay show output fields are from memory (to verify).

brief.situation: You are the database administrator at Haldane Freight, migrating the sales database from SQL Server to Azure SQL Managed Instance with Log Replay Service in continuous mode. Tonight is cutover: at 22:05 the application was stopped, a colleague took the log-tail backup and uploaded it. The managed instance should show it restored before you complete. The window ends at 23:00, when the application must come back on one side or the other.
handover: LRS has restored the full backup and 312 log backups from blob folder backups/sales/ since Monday.
The colleague uploaded the tail with a new script to keep tonight's files 'tidy'.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the blob folder LRS scans, the log-tail backup and the managed instance's restore position.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why the tail was not restored, what you did and in what order, and what changes for the next databases.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Connects LRS's position to the folder.
parts.modelAnswer: LRS's last restored file was the 21:55 log. The tail was uploaded to sales/cutover/, a nested folder; LRS reads only the database's flat folder, so it never saw it.

parts.label: Order
parts.modelAnswer: Copied the tail into sales/, waited until LRS showed it as the last restored file, then completed with it as the last backup. Completing first would have lost 20 minutes of orders permanently.

parts.label: Next
parts.modelAnswer: The upload script writes to the database's flat folder, and the runbook requires lastRestoredFileName to equal the tail before completing.

ordersMissing.headline: Complete only after the tail is restored
ordersMissing.body: In continuous mode the cutover is: stop the app, back up the tail, see it restored, then complete. Completing early loses the tail's transactions and closes the door on restoring them.

rolledBack.headline: LRS reads one flat folder per database
rolledBack.body: LRS builds the chain from the files in the database's folder, and nested folders are not supported. A file in a subfolder is invisible to it.

migrated.headline: Good: no lost transactions
migrated.body: You compared LRS's restore position with the files, found the tail in a nested folder, put it where LRS reads, waited for it to be restored, completed, checked the last orders, and fixed the runbook.

gaps.headline: Held, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the evidence before the change, the lasting step, the check, or the cause in the record.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: LRS has restored up to the 21:55 log, and the tail sits in a nested folder, which LRS does not scan. Put the tail in the database's flat folder, wait until LRS shows it restored, and only then complete the migration. Completing now brings the database online without the last 20 minutes of orders, and nothing more can be restored after completion. Re-uploading with the same script changes nothing. Fix the script and the runbook for the next databases.
